summary: In this excerpt from a novel, Mrs. Enderby arrives at Miss Craigie's house with Lexy Moran, who has been mistaken for Caroline, and sends Lexy upstairs with a trunk of Caroline's belongings. Alone in a bedroom, Lexy looks at Caroline's hat and coat and resolves to find Caroline, setting aside her own concerns about her job and Mrs. Enderby's attitude. She plans to spend her remaining money on the search.
one_line: Lexy Moran, mistaken for Caroline at Miss Craigie's house, resolves to find the missing Caroline.
key_facts: Mrs. Enderby pushes Miss Craigie inside and tells her that the girl Lexy is not Caroline, saying "I shall explain to you."
Miss Craigie exclaims "But it's not Caroline!" when she sees Lexy's face.
Mrs. Enderby instructs Miss Craigie to have no air of surprise and to allow the chauffeur to carry upstairs a small trunk.
Mrs. Enderby tells Lexy to "Turn your back!" and look out of the window while the chauffeur carries the trunk upstairs.
Miss Craigie is described as being in the habit of obeying Mrs. Enderby, and is described as bewildered.
Mrs. Enderby catches Lexy by the shoulder and says "Take off those things of my child's. Have you no heart?"
Miss Craigie leads Lexy up to a neat, prim little bedroom where the trunk stands already unlocked.
Lexy takes off Caroline's hat and coat and lays them on the bed, thinking "I wonder if I'll ever see her wearing them again!"
Lexy decides, "I'm going to find her!" and says she does not care what anyone else does or thinks.
Lexy has a little money due to her and means to use every penny of it to find Caroline.
Lexy washes her hands and face, brushes her hair, puts on her own hat and jacket, and goes downstairs again.
At the end of the excerpt, Mrs. Enderby is standing in the tiny hall.

entities.name: Caroline
entities.role: missing girl whose hat and coat Lexy finds; the one Lexy seeks

entities.name: Mrs. Enderby
